items.title: When do all iterates of $x^2 + a$ have maximal Galois group?
items.summary: We provide an (in our opinion) simpler proof of the main results of [Stoll1992,Li2020,Li2021] on the question for which integers $a$ the Galois groups of all iterates of $x^2 + a$ are maximal (equivalently, the associated arboreal Galois representation is surjective). At the same time, we extend the results to rational parameters $a$. The main result states that for a subset of rational numbers of relative density $1/2$ in the complement of a certain open interval, the maximality of the Galois group of the second iterate is sufficient for the arboreal Galois representation to be surjective. We also discuss experimental evidence suggesting that a similar statement involving the fourth iterate may hold in general. The results were obtained in collaboration with Claude (Anthropic's AI model); they are also formalized in Lean (except for the experimental evidence).

items.title: Singular points of envelopes and offsets: a transition from 2D to 3D
items.summary: We recall properties of the offsets of a (plane) kiss curve and their singularities, then we make a transition to 3D, considering the surface obtained by revolution of the kiss curve about one of its axes. When pos?sible, geometric constructions using automated methods are performed. This induces a need to focus on algebraic computations. Networking be?tween different kinds of software is of utmost importance, in order to use their respective strengths (dynamic geometry, dragging points, strong al?gebraic computations, etc.). A core difference between the 2D and 3D situations is that automated commands existing in 2D are not available in 3D. This makes the DGS less relevant in 3D than in 2D. In 3D, most of the work must be performed with the CAS. The singular points of a kiss curve in the plane are tacnodes (cusps) and crunodes (self-intersection). The singularities are not isolated anymore and cuspidal edges appear. In this setting, implicitization is a heavy endeavour and we need another technology, related to AI; we describe this briefly. The 2D activities have been proposed to in-service teachers learning towards an advanced degree.

items.title: BioXArena-Pro: a research-grade benchmark for autonomous biomedical machine learning agents
items.summary: Coding agents are increasingly proposed as autonomous builders of biomedical models, but existing benchmarks are small, near saturation or open to leaked information. We present BioXArena-Pro, 64 research-level modelling tasks from eight biomedical domains, each rebuilt from a published study; most hold out whole biological units such as species or cohorts. Across 22 agent configurations, the best scores 55.1 of 100, and the scaffold matters almost as much as the model. We re-ran a published method for every task: where the published recipe applies unchanged, the best agent and the methods tie; on rebuilt tasks the methods trail by 8.2 points, suggesting that agents gain by adapting to new data. Pretrained models (including biological foundation models) matter where the strongest agent uses them: forbidding them decreases its score on those tasks by 9 points. Every task was audited in several AI-assisted rounds and a final human review.
